scalars.revision: Distinct actual knowledge snapshot revision ordinal, initially 0; each changed name or background translation changes it once.
scalars.name: 0=Deebo, 1=Tibo, 2=Mira.
scalars.sourceName: Name token in the linked original segment; unchanged unlinked and other-listening sources are checked separately.
scalars.associatedName: Name token across associated item summary, fact and assertion text; all independently checked by adapter.
scalars.evidenceName: Name token in active remapped support quotes/source text (anchor validity separately represented).
scalars.changes: Number of actually committed non-no-op replacement operations, 0..2.
scalars.sourceVersion: Observed replacement generation of linked source, 0..2; an ordinal, not a production DB column.
scalars.associatedVersion: Observed replacement generation of associated knowledge/fact/assertion records, 0..2.
scalars.evidenceVersion: Observed replacement generation of active supports, 0..2.
scalars.anchorValid: All active support hashes, safe-integer UTF-16 bounds and quotes match current linked source. Invalidated source supports do not change the knowledge revision.
scalars.background: none, revision (linked translation completion), or anchor (active source support corruption), each at most once.
scalars.stalePreserved: Historical stale support rows equal baseline exactly.
scalars.scopePreserved: Unlinked segment and entire unrelated listening's business rows equal baseline exactly.
scalars.identitiesPreserved: Item/fact/relation/assertion/support IDs and relation endpoints equal baseline.

mapSemantics.rawName: Exact input string; padding is significant for the fingerprint despite equal trimmed target.
mapSemantics.receiptRawName: Symbolic raw input of original successful operation; bind to actual SHA256(JSON.stringify(['name_replace',rawName,actualRevision])).
mapSemantics.receiptInputRevision: Original submitted revision ordinal, persisted on receipt; never updated on replay.
mapSemantics.receiptCommitRevision: Observed snapshot ordinal immediately after original commit, retained by adapter; not a new persisted field.
mapSemantics.receiptOwner: Attempt slot that first committed the ID, -1 if none; observation bookkeeping, not a DB field.
mapSemantics.commits: Actually committed successful operation count per ID, 0 or1; no-op counts as commit.

adapter.initial: Synthetic fixture from seedNameReplacement(graph:true), historical stale support, another listening, linked translation eligible for one update. Both attempts unused. No edit receipts. No override: override and legacy-codec rules reuse KEJ-69/70.
adapter.prepare: Own new picks name actor+1, same uses current name; freeze current snapshot revision. In reuse config actor1 explicitly copies actor0 ID+body (exact), adds surrounding raw-name spaces (raw_mismatch), or keeps raw name with a changed current revision (revision_mismatch). Actor0 must have sent before actor1 reuses its ID. No transport call at prepare.
adapter.send: One explicit POST queued at real test-only HTTP holding proxy. Each attempt sends once. No automatic retry.
adapter.transaction: One synchronous actual handler/store call, including best-effort synchronous notification. Receipt lookup first; exact replay returns stored receipt and changed=false before checking stale revision/anchor. Associated-write fault only triggers on changed replacements; no-op skips associated writes and still succeeds. Receipt-write fault triggers on every new receipt, including no-op; duplicate paths do not write and ignore injected write faults. Triggered write faults abort actual SQLite transaction; retain complete before/after table rows. No await inside the transaction.
adapter.lookup: GET only. Existing receipt gives phase saved/reply receipt; unlike POST ok this only establishes the original stored ID outcome. Do not assert deliberately mismatched retry body succeeded. Browser UUID generation prevents ordinary UI collision; real browser is separately required.
adapter.refresh: Fresh GET after outcome; phase done, actual latest name and revision. It may stand for reopening a dialog, but this adapter alone is not browser evidence.
adapter.background_change: revision changes linked translation only; anchor changes an active support's quote/source hash only, leaving knowledge snapshot revision equal. Both happen between complete SQLite calls.
adapter.mutations: ignore_fingerprint maps to actual removed fingerprint guard; partial_rollback and receipt_without_commit represent possible split-transaction failures. Revision/anchor guards are inherited boundary coverage, not new production changes.

scope.fingerprint: Exact finite input tuple, not a proof of SHA256 collision freedom. IDs are scoped to one listening/item; cross-scope rejection requires implementation regression.
scope.coordinates: Finite model abstracts transformed UTF-16 content by symbols. Coordinate laws are the separate KEJ-70 Lean/name-interval profile and real replay comparisons.
scope.liveness: No liveness claim. Eventual completion needs fair dispatch/delivery and available recovery reads; permanent unavailability is allowed.
exclusions: Legacy revision/override state combinations already covered in KEJ-69/70
